newsitem.title: INDIA: India 1995/96 household investment in shares falls.
newsitem.headline: India 1995/96 household investment in shares falls.

text.p: Indian household investment in the stock markets fell to 0.5 percent of GDP in 1995/96 (April-March) from 1.3 percent in 1994/95, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said on Monday.

"Household investment in shares and debentures, including units of the Unit Trust of India (UTI), which had declined from 147.72 billion rupees during 1993/94 (April-March) to 123.69 billion in 1994/95 is expected to have decelerated further to 61.42 billion rupees in 1995/96," the RBI said.

In its "Report on Currency and Finance 1995/96", the RBI attributed the development to a downtrend in Indian capital markets and the dismal performance of mutual funds including the state-run UTI, the largest mutual fund.

As a result, the share of household investment in shares and debentures fell sharply to 4.9 percent of gross household financial savings from 8.9 percent in 1994/95 and 13.5 percent in 1993/94, the RBI report said.
It said household investment in UTI units plunged to 2.62 billion rupees in 1995/96 from 39.08 billion rupees in 1994/95 and 47.05 billion rupees in 1993/94.
Mobilisation by other mutual funds fell sharply to 3.51 billion rupees in 1995/96 from 8.38 billion rupees in 1994/95 and 12.72 billion rupees in 1993/94, the report said.

"The household sector's direct investment in equities and debentures of private corporate business, after declining from 74.43 billion rupees in 1993/94 to 73.77 billion rupees in 1994/95, further declined to 59.57 billion rupees in 1995/96."
State-run firms raised 1.63 billion rupees of household financial savings in 1995/96 through bond issues against 1.05 billion rupees in 1994/95 and 5.04 billion rupees in 1993-94.
